findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics if the file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8.
findings.failure_mode: entire process aborts with a panic instead of returning a typed I/O error that the caller can handle, retry, or report
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError::Io> and use map_err or ? to propagate fs::read_to_string errors

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric or out-of-range value in the CSV field.
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed CSV line (e.g. whitespace, negative sign, decimal point, or text) crashes the entire packet load with a panic
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError::Parse> and use map_err on parse::<u32>() to produce a typed ParseError

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy widening-to-narrow cast that silently truncates values above 65535.
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 wraps to 34464 in the Record, corrupting the domain value with no error or warning
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| PacketError::Overflow) instead of as u16, returning a typed Overflow error when the value exceeds u16::MAX

findings.problem: parts[0] is an unchecked Vec index into a split result. Any CSV line with zero fields (empty line) will panic.
findings.failure_mode: an empty or whitespace-only CSV line causes an IndexOutOfBounds panic in the println! macro
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) with .ok_or() or pattern-match the split result length before indexing

findings.problem: parts[1] is an unchecked Vec index. Any CSV line with only one field (no comma) will panic.
findings.failure_mode: a line like "sensor_temp" with no comma and no second field crashes the packet loader with an IndexOutOfBounds panic
findings.fix: use parts.get(1) with .ok_or(PacketError::MalformedLine) or check parts.len() >= 2 before access

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is console I/O embedded inside data-parsing logic. This is a side effect leaking into what should be pure data construction.
findings.failure_mode: the function produces observable I/O side effects during data processing, breaking the Functional Core / Imperative Shell separation. Tests cannot suppress stdout, and the side effect is not part of the return contract.
findings.fix: remove the println! entirely; if diagnostics are needed, push them to the shell boundary as a separate side-effect function or pass a logging callback

findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println!), CSV parsing, and domain object construction into a single function with no error return type.
findings.failure_mode: the shell (I/O) and core (parsing/construction) are inseparable. Callers cannot inject mock data, cannot handle specific error categories, and cannot separate parsing from disk access. The function also has no Result type, so all failures surface as panics.
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, PacketError> and (2) a shell fn load_packets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> that handles file I/O and delegates to parse_record

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec<String> per line with no capacity bound, no max_items check, and no try_reserve. The outer .collect() on the map iterator also has no capacity bound.
findings.failure_mode: a single CSV line with thousands of comma-separated fields, or a CSV file with millions of lines, causes unbounded heap allocation with no graceful degradation or allocation failure handling
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for the two-field grammar, avoid intermediate Vec per line, and add try_reserve(max_lines) on the outer Vec after validating max_items against a trusted cap

findings.problem: Uses line.split(',').map(...).collect() to build a Vec<String> for a two-field CSV record. The SKILL mandates split_once(',') for one-separator grammars.
findings.failure_mode: allocates two intermediate Strings per field (one for each trimmed copy) plus the Vec container, all to extract exactly two values. This is unnecessary allocation that increases memory pressure and cache churn compared to split_once which yields two &str references.
findings.fix: replace with let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(PacketError::MalformedLine)?; then parse value_str directly

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper and no error enum. All failure modes (file not found, I/O error, malformed CSV, parse failure, overflow) are collapsed into panic surfaces via unwrap().
findings.failure_mode: callers have zero ability to distinguish between a missing file, a corrupted line, an out-of-range number, or a truncation overflow. Error handling is entirely reactive (catch panics) rather than proactive (match typed errors).
findings.fix: define enum PacketError { Io(std::io::Error), MalformedLine, Parse(std::num::ParseIntError), Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError>
